explanation: The act where God takes back the exiled Israelites as an olive branch into the true faith, so that they once again become part of God's people.
A symbol of true Israel or the church, where both Jews and Gentiles are grafted together through faith in Christ.
Represents the Gentiles who were not part of the original covenant but are now grafted into God's blessing by receiving Jesus.
Refers to the Jewish roots or Abraham and his descendants as the foundation of true Israel; Gentiles draw nourishment from this heritage.
Describes the temporary blindness and resistance many Israelites show toward the gospel before God's grace turns back to them all.
The concept that the entire nation of Israel, not just a part, will be saved when the time comes for God's completed plans.
God's unmerited favor and mercy that offers salvation to both Jews and Gentiles without any merit on humanity's part.
Describes that God's gifts and calling are eternal and cannot be withdrawn, even if people fall into sin or doubt.
